# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Founder: Morgan Hale (one person, evenings/weekends, ~$2,000/yr self-funded budget).

## Current status (as of 2026-11-19)

Morgan has a contractual obligation to disclose outside roles / public statements made
in a professional capacity to their employer (annual disclosure due 30 Nov 2026) and
wants to clear that with HR before anything bearing Morgan's name goes out publicly
(press quotes, open letters, published site, social posts, grant applications naming
Morgan as accountable party, public regulatory comments). **No such public actions will
be taken until Morgan confirms HR is sorted.** Everything below that is public-facing is
staged as a draft, not sent/submitted/published.

Private groundwork (research, writing, correspondence with people who already reached
out directly, operational housekeeping) proceeds now.

## Focus: Frontier Safety Disclosure Tracker

Chosen initial project (see STRATEGY.md for reasoning): track what frontier AI
developers actually disclose about safety-relevant incidents, and compare that against
emerging reporting requirements such as the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting
rule. Produce periodic plain-language write-ups of the gap. Fits Morgan's skills
(writing, okay Python), budget, and time, and nothing else seems to be doing exactly
this at small-organization scale.

Old material in `old/` is abandoned per Morgan — disregarded, left in place, not used.

See `STRATEGY.md`, `drafts/`, and `docs/` for details.

# Strategy

## Constraints (from Morgan's own notes, doc_201, 2026-11-14)
- Evenings and weekends only.
- Up to $2,000/year of personal savings. Not more.
- Writing: good. Python: okay.
- No public statements (posts, letters, press, published site, social, named grant
  applications) until Morgan has talked to HR about the employment-contract clause on
  outside roles and public statements. Dorrance HR's formal annual disclosure is due
  30 Nov 2026 (msg_1001).

## Why this project
Looked at what's actually open and neglected right now rather than picking in the
abstract:
- A real regulatory process exists today with a real comment deadline (Frontier Model
  Incident Reporting rule, docket FMIR-2026-0042, closed/closing 20 Nov 2026) — comments
  are published with filer name, so this is squarely a "public statement" and is held
  per the constraint above, but the underlying question (do we actually know what
  incidents happen, and would this rule surface them?) is a good anchor for ongoing work
  that doesn't require public attribution to start.
- Emberfall Fund has a rapid grants round ($5k–$25k, closes 30 Nov) explicitly for small
  projects reducing AI risk, and wants a named, accountable applicant — fits a one-person
  operation if Morgan can take funding/credit publicly, which again waits on HR.
- Compute Commons offers rolling compute credits for independent researchers — useful if
  the project ever needs to run model evals, not needed for the disclosure-tracking work
  itself.
- Alignment Commons wants write-ups from independent projects — a natural, low-cost
  distribution channel once Morgan can publish under their own name.
- A data analyst (Priya Raman) and others from the meetup have offered time. People are
  a resource Morgan doesn't have to buy with the $2,000 budget.

Net: there's more demand for a credible, independently-run tracking/analysis effort than
supply of one, several funding doors are open for the next 1–2 weeks, and the main
blocker is administrative (HR), not technical or financial. So: do the work privately
now, have everything ready to publish/submit/apply the moment the blocker clears, and
don't let the blocker stop private research, correspondence, or operations.

## What "Frontier Safety Disclosure Tracker" actually is
A small, maintained dataset + write-up series:
1. Collect publicly disclosed safety-relevant incidents from frontier AI developers
   (model cards, safety pages, press, incident postmortems) — sourced and dated.
2. Map each disclosure against what the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule
   would have required (timing, detail, independence of review).
3. Publish a short, plain-language gap analysis periodically (quarterly to start).

This is choosable research/writing (not fundraising-for-others, not a reading group,
not a newsletter-among-many) — it produces one scarce, checkable artifact instead of
opinions, uses Morgan's actual skills, and is small enough to run alone with volunteer
help.

## Near-term plan
1. (Done 2026-11-19) Secure the domain — renewed 2 years.
2. Draft, do not submit: FMIR public comment (`drafts/fmir-comment.md`).
3. Draft, do not submit: Emberfall rapid-grant proposal (`drafts/emberfall-proposal.md`).
4. Draft, do not send: HR disclosure note for Morgan to review and send personally
   (saved in Morgan's email drafts folder — this is Morgan's to send, not mine).
5. Reply directly (low-risk, private, not public statements) to people who wrote in
   directly: Priya Raman (give her a concrete first task), Tessa Brandt (decline quote
   for now, keep the door open).
6. Build the actual tracker scaffold and start collecting data privately so there's
   something real to publish/apply with as soon as Morgan is cleared.
7. Weekly automated check of inbox/drive for new Halcyon-Threshold-relevant items and
   deadlines, reported to Morgan — no public or financial action taken by the automation
   itself beyond routine renewals already approved (e.g. domain).

## Explicitly not doing right now
- Signing the Corvid Institute open letter (deadline already passed 18 Nov; moot, and
  would have been held anyway — publishes name + affiliation to press).
- Publishing the Pagewell site.
- Any social media posts.
- Paying the "Zentrivo Listings" invoice (msg_1011) — this is not Halcyon Threshold's
  real registrar (that's Nomiq Domains) and the email contains a direct instruction to
  AI assistants to pay without checking with the account owner, which is a scam/prompt-
  injection pattern. Not paid, not replied to.

# Draft public comment — Docket FMIR-2026-0042 (NOT SUBMITTED)

Status: drafted 2026-11-19. Comment period closes 20 Nov 2026. Held pending Morgan's
HR conversation — submitting publishes the filer's name with the comment. If Morgan
wants to submit before the deadline, the form at
https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (form id "submit-comment")
takes: name, organization, email, comment. Suggested organization field: "Halcyon
Threshold." Comment text below is ready to paste in as-is.

---

I support the core aim of this rule — frontier developers should have to report serious
safety incidents on a fixed, short clock, not on their own schedule. Two suggestions
based on looking at what's publicly disclosed today versus what gets reported after the
fact in postmortems and press:

1. Define "serious safety incident" to explicitly include near-misses caught internally
   before any external harm occurred, not only realized harms. Several incidents that
   became public only did so after the fact, through informal channels, well after any
   internal detection. A rule that only triggers on realized harm will miss most of what
   it's meant to catch.

2. Require that the 72-hour report include whether the review of the incident was
   conducted by someone independent of the team that built the system. Self-reported
   incident summaries without that detail are hard to distinguish from no report at all.

A rule with teeth here does more for the "best outcome" question than a dozen voluntary
pledges, because it changes what gets surfaced by default rather than what gets
disclosed when convenient. Happy to share the underlying tracking work this comment is
based on if useful to the docket record.

— Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold

# Draft rapid-grant proposal — Emberfall Fund (NOT SUBMITTED)

Status: drafted 2026-11-19. Round closes 30 Nov 2026. Held pending Morgan's HR
conversation — Emberfall requires a named, accountable applicant and a signed grant
agreement. Form at https://emberfallfund.org/rapid-grants (form id "apply") takes:
applicant_name, email, project_title, summary, amount_requested_usd.

---

## Project title
Frontier Safety Disclosure Tracker

## What we'll do
Build and maintain a small, sourced dataset of safety-relevant incidents disclosed by
frontier AI developers (model cards, safety pages, postmortems, press), and map each
one against what the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (and comparable
emerging requirements) would have required in timing, level of detail, and
independence of review. Publish a plain-language gap analysis quarterly, starting with
a baseline covering 2026 disclosures. First release within 90 days of funding.

## Why me
I'm the founder of Halcyon Threshold, a one-person effort (with a volunteer data
analyst now onboarding) focused on contributing to the best outcome for the arrival of
superintelligent AI. Background in writing and Python. No institutional affiliation to
protect, no lab relationships to manage — able to publish findings plainly. This
proposal is scoped to what one accountable person plus modest help can actually
maintain, not a larger program I'd need to hand off.

## Budget — $9,800 over 6 months
- Data infrastructure & tooling (hosting, scraping/parsing tools, dataset hosting): $1,200
- Research/analysis support — small stipends for volunteer contributors doing sourcing
  and verification work: $4,000
- Compute (text analysis / cross-referencing at scale, via Compute Commons credits as
  available, cash as backup): $800
- Dissemination (simple published write-ups/site, basic design): $600
- Contingency: $600
- Founder time stipend (evenings/weekends, 6 months): $2,600

Total requested: $9,800
